sect1.title: elogind-&elogind-version;
sect1.sect2:
Introduction to elogind
The elogind package is an extracted "logind" from Systemd, including the daemon and some other Systemd projects like UserDB. It integrates with to track all the users logged in to a system, and whether they are logged in graphically, on the console, or remotely. It exposes this information via the standard org.freedesktop.login1 D-Bus interface, and also through the file system using Systemd's standard /run/systemd layout.

sect2.title: Installation of elogind
sect2.para: Install elogind by running the following commands:

screen.userinput:
mkdir build && cd build &&
meson setup --prefix=/usr \ --buildtype=release \ -D docdir=/usr/share/doc/elogind-&elogind-version; \ -D cgroup-controller=elogind \ -D dev-kvm-mode=0660 \ -D dbuspolicydir=/etc/dbus-1/system.d \ .. && ninja
ninja install && ln -sfv libelogind.pc /usr/lib/pkgconfig/libsystemd.pc && ln -sfvn elogind /usr/include/systemd

sect2.title: lib32 Installation of elogind
sect2.para: Install lib32-elogind by running the following commands:

screen.userinput: rm -rf * && meson setup --prefix=/usr \ --buildtype=release \ --cross-file=lib32 \ -D cgroup-controller=elogind \ -D dev-kvm-mode=0660 \ -D dbuspolicydir=/etc/dbus-1/system.d \ .. && ninja
DESTDIR=$PWD/DESTDIR ninja install && cp -vR DESTDIR/usr/lib32/* /usr/lib32 && rm -rf DESTDIR && ln -sfv libelogind.pc /usr/lib32/pkgconfig/libsystemd.pc && ldconfig

sect1.sect2:
Command Explanations
&options-meson;
-D docdir=/usr/share/doc/elogind-&elogind-version;: This is needed to install documentation in a versioned directory.
-D cgroup-controller=elogind: This switch is necessary to build this package when the kernel is not built with CONFIG_CGROUPS enabled. Note that elogind strictly needs a kernel with CONFIG_CGROUPS enabled at runtime, but this switch will allow building the package first.
-D dbuspolicydir=/etc/dbus-1/system.d: This switch sets the location of the D-Bus policy directory.
-D dev-kvm-mode=0660: The LFS udev rule sets the mode of /dev/kvm to 0660. This option ensures the elogind udev rules consistent with the LFS configuration.
-D default-kill-user-processes=false: Determines whether the processes of a user should be killed when the user logs out. The default is true, but this defeats the traditional use of screen or tmux. This can also be changed in the configuration file (see below).
ln -s ...: These commands install symlinks so that software packages can find the systemd-compatible library and headers.

sect3.title: Configuration Information
sect3.para: The installed file /etc/elogind/logind.conf contains all the possible options with their defaults, commented out. You may wish to disable automatically killing user processes when the user logs out. You can do so as the &root; user:

Each user will need to register a user session using Linux-PAM at login. The /etc/pam.d/system-session file needs to be modified and a new file must be created in order for elogind to work correctly. Run the following commands as the root user:

screen.userinput:
cat >> /etc/pam.d/system-session << "EOF" && # Begin elogind addition
session required pam_loginuid.so session optional pam_elogind.so
# End elogind addition EOF cat > /etc/pam.d/elogind-user << "EOF" # Begin /etc/pam.d/elogind-user
account required pam_access.so account include system-account
session required pam_env.so session required pam_limits.so session required pam_unix.so session required pam_loginuid.so session optional pam_keyinit.so force revoke session optional pam_elogind.so
auth required pam_deny.so password required pam_deny.so
# End /etc/pam.d/elogind-user EOF

sect3.para: This package provides a Name Service Switch (NSS) module. Previously, a Systemd-less system didn't have a dedicated NSS module used for better name resolution, while Systemd systems have one that is tightly ingrained with that software suite. Now, such a module is provided. In order to use it, the /etc/nsswitch.conf file that was installed in LFS must be altered. Overwrite the file as the &root; user:

screen.userinput:
cat > /etc/nsswitch.conf << "EOF" && # Begin /etc/nsswitch.conf
passwd: files elogind group: files elogind shadow: files elogind
hosts: files dns networks: files
protocols: files services: files ethers: files rpc: files
# End /etc/nsswitch.conf EOF

note.para: The myhostname, mymachines, and resolve NSS modules are still not provided (they come from Systemd). The installed file cannot use them yet.
